OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          pattern: '(?s).*\S.*'
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized
            to E.164 form; a leading '+' and country code are kept when present, otherwise
            country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is dropped from the
            national digits. Spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped and the result must
            be a '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must
            be a syntactically valid address and is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: The date the pet owner was registered. Optional on create; when
            omitted it defaults to the server's current date. Returned in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: When true on create, allows registering this owner even if another
            owner already has the same last name and postal address (compared
            case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace) because they share a household.
            Otherwise such a request is rejected with 409 Conflict. Request-only; not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'Franklin, George'
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: The upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'G.F.'
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: The owner's customer code, formatted '<CITY3>-<LAST3>-<NNNN>' where CITY3
                is the upper-cased first three letters of city, LAST3 the upper-cased first three
                letters of lastName and NNNN a per-city 4-digit zero-padded sequence equal to one
                more than the number of owners already registered in that city.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'SYD-SMI-0007'
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: A stable identifier shared by all owners in the same household, i.e.
                owners with the same last name and postal address (compared case-insensitively
                with collapsed whitespace). Owners registered with 'sharesHousehold' set share
                this value.
              type: string
              readOnly: true
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: The single derived key used for duplicate detection, formed as
                'normalizedTelephone|email|householdId' (the email segment is empty when no email
                is present, the householdId segment is empty when it has not yet been assigned).
                A create is rejected with 409 Conflict only when a new owner's whole identityKey
                equals an existing owner's; because the telephone is part of the key, two members
                of the same household with different telephones have different keys and are both
                allowed.
              type: string

## Summary

I prepared the ground for the upcoming postcode feature without implementing it.

**What I found:** The city→region table the new feature needs (Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD, else UNKNOWN) *already exists* in this codebase — but inlined as a ternary chain buried inside `OwnerMapper`'s `locality` mapping expression. Implemented directly, `isPostcodeValidForCity` (and `addOwner`) would have to re-derive that same region from the city, duplicating this logic. That duplication is the "complexity these classes can't hold comfortably."

**What I changed** (pure, behavior-preserving extraction):

1. **`Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient getRegion()` derived getter, sitting right alongside the existing derived getters (`getMembershipLevel`, `getContactPreference`) and following their exact style and javadoc convention. It reproduces the region derivation identically (same case-sensitive `equals`, same outputs).

2. **`OwnerMapper.java`** — replaced the inline ternary in the `locality` mapping with `expression = "java(owner.getRegion())"`.

**Why this is the natural prep:** The city→region concept now has a single, discoverable home on the domain object, consistent with how `Owner` already exposes derived attributes. When the postcode change lands, `isPostcodeValidForCity` becomes a straightforward "look up the region, check the range" — reusing `owner.getRegion()` instead of re-deriving it — and `addOwner` gains just one guard clause matching its existing 400-check style. No region logic gets duplicated across the model, the mapper, and the controller.

**Behaviour preserved exactly:** `locality` in API responses is derived identically; I verified the test outcome is bit-for-bit the same as the original code (1 pass / 2 pre-existing postcode failures).

One note on the tests: `AcceptanceTest`'s `coreStoresValidPostcode` and `errorRejectsMalformedPostcode` are the acceptance tests *for the upcoming change* and are red until that feature is implemented — which this task explicitly told me not to do. They fail identically before and after my refactoring, so I've left them as-is rather than implementing the feature to make them green.
